title: Bind field names and types into the evidence seal
evidence: compute_merkle_root hashes only str(val) or serialized container values, then sorts leaf hashes. Keys are excluded and order is discarded. For example {author:A,text:B} and {author:B,text:A} yield the same leaf multiset; scalar 1 and string 1 also have identical leaf bytes. Main inserts this root as merkle_seal at lines 2935–2940.
trigger: Swap two scalar values between evidence fields, rename a field, or change a scalar type while retaining its string representation.
impact: The advertised evidence seal cannot detect semantic tampering with field associations or scalar types.

title: Namespace vault record IDs by platform and instance
evidence: save_to_vault selects data.id as record_id, table defines record_id alone as PRIMARY KEY, and INSERT OR REPLACE discards the existing record. Mastodon fetch_status emits status_id as id (line 1909) without instance namespace.
trigger: Save two statuses with the same local numeric ID from different Mastodon instances into the shared vault.
impact: The second capture silently replaces the first source record and its forensic content.

title: Emit a valid JSON container for batch output
evidence: For --format json each item is json.dumps(extracted_data), but final_output joins all_reports with a Markdown separator. The --batch option can produce two or more items.
trigger: Run a batch with at least two successfully extracted URLs and --format json.
impact: Output is not a JSON document and cannot be parsed by downstream JSON tooling.

title: Do not label watch-page text as an audio transcript
evidence: YouTubeAdapter fetches the video watch URL through r.jina.ai, puts the entire first 10000 body characters into transcript_text, and reports it under Transcripción de Audio at line 2301. No captions or audio transcription stage exists in the adapter.
trigger: Fetch a video through this adapter.
impact: Page metadata and unrelated watch-page text can be presented and analyzed as words spoken in the video.

title: Label regex matches as candidate facts rather than verified facts
evidence: EpistemicClassifier matches references such as RFC, sha256 or a legal keyword and increments hechos_verificados, which the Markdown report renders as Hechos Verificados at line 2462. There is no source retrieval, evidence validation or truth check in classify_text.
trigger: Classify a false sentence that includes a matching reference keyword.
impact: The report presents unverified textual claims as verified evidence.

title: JSON output skips requested claim export
evidence: run_single_cycle returns immediately for json_output at 244-246; export_claims is processed only at 277-280.
trigger: Invoke the CLI with --json --export-claims PATH and a cycle containing claim receipts.
impact: The command exits successfully without creating the explicitly requested receipt file.

title: Manifest inspector certifies properties it never checks
evidence: The branch condition at 118 checks native mode, address alignment, and halt state, then prints Landauer Bound OK and Fail-Stop Gate OK. It does not test either property or even include is_consistent in acceptance.
trigger: Run --inspect-manifest with a native aligned nonhalted manifest.
impact: CLI presents unsupported physical and fail-stop guarantees as checked invariants.

title: Inference verifier proves only a freely chosen multiplication witness
evidence: verify_inference_payload verifies InferenceConstraint; build.rs:8-16 constrains only private weight * public nonce == public expected_hash. No model, input, output or authorized weight commitment is constrained. stress_test.rs:29-45 constructs proofs of precisely this relation.
trigger: A consumer interprets true from verify_inference_payload as evidence of model inference. For every nonzero nonce and field hash a witness weight = hash / nonce exists.
impact: A valid proof establishes no inference correctness or binding to a particular model. Only the local verifier and stress harness were traced; no production effect bypass is claimed.

title: Groth16 setup randomness is publicly reproducible
evidence: get_verifying_key seeds ChaCha20Rng with a literal public constant and runs Groth16::setup; src/bin/stress_test.rs:19-26 regenerates the same setup for its prover.
trigger: This verifying key is used as a security boundary beyond an isolated demonstration.
impact: Setup secret randomness can be reconstructed by any party; this cannot provide the secret setup assumptions of Groth16. No forged proof was generated in this audit.

title: Seeded FL014 experiment uses process-randomized hash for decisions
evidence: Acceptance uses hash((patch.patch_id, "safe")); known/unseen bypass branches use the same pattern at 181 and 188. Dataset RNG seeding does not seed Python string hashing.
trigger: Run the experiment or tests in separate interpreters with different default hash seeds.
impact: Decisions and gap change despite fixed dataset seeds; numerical assertions in tests/test_fl014_holdout_poc.py depend on uncontrolled randomness.

title: Artifact identity comparison checks only a prefix
evidence: has_identity_mismatch = not patch.patch_id.startswith("PATCH-"); dynamic_result.patch_id and code_diff identity are never compared.
trigger: Pass PATCH-0001 with a DynamicExecutionResult for PATCH-0002.
impact: The simulated broker reports no identity mismatch, so the example does not check the artifact-binding invariant it advertises.

title: Non-persist witness digest silently replaces SHA256 with XOR
evidence: cfg(not(cortex-persist)) ignores domain and XOR-folds payload into32bytes; PhysicalResourceWitness uses it at1689.
trigger: Library built without cortex-persist; same-inode64byte content mutated at positions0 and32 by toggling low bit from zero to one.
impact: Both paired contributions change identically so digest remains unchanged; physical witness can miss content mutation. This is an API configuration issue, not proof of a deployed bypass.

title: Evidence digest omits observer visibility and witness identity fields
evidence: to_cortex_evidence hashes selected fields but excludes observer_visibility, threat_model_limitations, witness inodes and broker_authorized_mutation while storing them in artifact.
trigger: Two reports differ only in omitted visibility/limitations or witness inode fields.
impact: Distinct evidence artifacts share digest; digest cannot authenticate claimed complete artifact.

title: New ATMS premises bypass an already established unconditional contradiction
evidence: add_premise inserts label {empty} without checking nogoods (171-178); contradict([]) creates empty nogood via contributions (330,350) and add_nogood; is_believed and contradiction_free test only label nonemptiness (230-231,284-285).
trigger: Call contradict(&[]), then add_premise("p"), then contradiction_free(p) before another propagation.
impact: Returns contradiction-free for a node in an ATMS where every environment is inconsistent, violating its public consistency claim.

title: Telemetry stop cancels the worker without draining pending events
evidence: stop docstring promises draining at 55 but cancels at 57, awaits the cancelled worker and clears it at 62; it never awaits queue.join or consumes remaining items.
trigger: Ingest events and immediately stop before the background worker has consumed them.
impact: Queued events remain unprocessed when stop returns, contrary to the shutdown contract.

title: Sequence validator accepts an empty normalized sequence
evidence: Nonempty input is checked before upper().strip(); no emptiness check follows. Empty invalid_chars passes, seq_len=0 returns is_valid=True (87–116).
trigger: Call validate_sequence with a nonempty whitespace-only sequence string.
impact: Invalid empty biological input receives a valid result and the digest of empty bytes.

title: Enforce the advertised subprocess timeout
evidence: _call_tool accepts timeout=15 at 21 but never uses it; blocking readline at 52 and 77 and stderr.read at 54/79 have no deadline.
trigger: The Node MCP process starts but never emits a complete initialization/tool response, or keeps stderr open after stdout closes.
impact: CLI call hangs indefinitely and never reaches finally to terminate the child.

title: DAG failure releases global lock while sibling tasks still execute
evidence: asyncio.gather propagates the first exception; ThermalLock exits immediately; sibling coroutines have no cancellation or draining in finally.
trigger: Run independent tasks where one raises while another awaits an operation, with caller catching the error and keeping the loop alive.
impact: The remaining task continues after lock removal, permitting another scheduler run to overlap protected work.

title: Avoid treating missing failure logs as proof of all invariants
evidence: Tutorial states that absence of CRITICAL HALT in a log is positive proof that execution maintained all invariants. No completeness or trusted monitoring premise accompanies the claim.
trigger: Use tutorial guidance to accept an incomplete log or a run with an uninstrumented defect.
impact: Readers are instructed to certify correctness from absence of an error message, exceeding the evidence supplied.

title: Launcher serves an absent UI directory
evidence: UI_DIR points to repository-root ui; metadata inspection shows ui, ui/index.html and ui/wizard.html absent. Handler maps / to wizard.html or index.html.
trigger: Start launcher and open its default URL in this checkout.
impact: The primary IDE and setup wizard return file-not-found.

title: Demo reports universal containment from two fixed simulated traces
evidence: The loop at 97-101 only chooses between two constant traces. verify_trace has no rejection branch for unknown operations (56-74), and its successful message claims Z3 although no solver is invoked. Final output claims 100% subordination and no leaks to Ring-0.
trigger: Run the demonstration or use its terminal verdict as security evidence.
impact: Evidence overstates an isolated Python simulator as containment of external LLMs and Ring-0; an unknown opcode is silently accepted by this simulator. No production execution bypass is alleged.

title: Use durable synchronous mode in trace-ledger schema
evidence: Schema explicitly sets WAL plus synchronous=NORMAL. goal_trace_ingestor.py:24-29 executes this schema on its connection before inserting traces.
trigger: Persist a trace and subsequently suffer power loss before WAL synchronization.
impact: Acknowledged traces can lose durability; this contradicts the canonical synchronous=FULL persistence requirement.

title: Skill auditor passes when no skill directories exist
evidence: Search roots are hardcoded ~/BABYLON-60/.agents/skills and ~/.gemini/config/skills (20-23); absent roots are skipped; empty files generates no errors and returns PASS.
trigger: Run on a checkout elsewhere with neither legacy directory populated.
impact: Quality gate reports 100% compliance for zero inspected skills, leaving the actual workspace skill library unchecked.

title: Archived sitrep presents constant success values as independent attestation
evidence: The report asserts ATTESTED_C5_REAL and health_index 98.6. Traced generator scripts/c5_sharur/sharur_100_conversation_reporters.py:341-345 assigns both literals and PASS without checks; lines 96-100 and 148-152 similarly emit constant sync/isolation successes, serialized by the reporter.
trigger: Reading the archived sitrep as evidence of security or workspace isolation.
impact: The recorded certification and several PASS assertions cannot establish the claimed properties because the generating branches do not measure them. Preserve as unverified historical output rather than attested evidence.

title: Documentation distiller targets a fixed obsolete checkout
evidence: WORKSPACE is /Users/borjafernandezangulo/BABYLON-60; all input/output paths derive from it, while frozen manifest root is /Users/borjafernandezangulo/10_PROJECTS/BABYLON-60.
trigger: Invoke this script from the assigned checkout or a fresh clone elsewhere.
impact: It reads/writes a different checkout if that path exists, or fails to find docs and cannot generate the intended package; no root argument or discovery is offered.

title: Zero-operation benchmark indexes an empty latency vector
evidence: CLI accepts std::stoull(argv[1]); when total_ops is 0 neither loop records samples, yet percentile indexing and back() are unconditional.
trigger: Run the standalone benchmark with argument 0.
impact: Undefined behavior or crash instead of rejecting invalid benchmark input.

title: Scheduled-operation deduplication commits success before operation
evidence: Sample writes execution ID at 110 before awaiting performIdempotentOperation at 111.
trigger: Operation rejects after the KV put succeeds and the same execution is retried.
impact: Retry sees existing marker at 102-107 and skips the failed operation permanently; example loses work.

title: Audio example mutates persistent DSP state during rendering
evidence: Line 36 memoizes a mutable ballisticState once; lines 53-56 pass it into extractBands on every render. SpectralFlux.ts:95-99 overwrites prevSpectrum and applies ballistics; :51-60 incorporates and updates smoothedValues.
trigger: Render the same frame after a different preceding frame, seek backwards, or rerender the same component/frame.
impact: Onset and smoothed band values depend on render history rather than only frame and input audio. Preview seeking and independently rendered segments can produce differing camera and glow values for the same frame.

title: Do not certify hardware and SLSA properties without evidence
evidence: generate_scitt_attestation hardcodes Apple Silicon, Secure Enclave TRNG, zero_leakage_certified=True and SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_3; returned receipt consists only of statement and its SHA-256 digest, with no signing, hardware lookup or provenance verification.
trigger: Invoke the standalone CLI on any directory, including a non-Git directory (which silently receives an all-zero commit).
impact: Exported provenance represents unmeasured and unauthenticated security properties as certified.

title: Certificate panel presents static text as verified hardware attestation
evidence: Step 3 contains a hard-coded VERIFIED token and immutable Secure Enclave signature claims; setStep exposes it directly and launchWorkbench only logs and alerts.
trigger: Open the SCITT Attestation tab without any backend result.
impact: The UI displays a verified certificate without signature or receipt verification. This is a presentation claim defect; no actual protected execution is demonstrated.
